brief: The far bank's second door is shut on the clock. `overDeck` sends east agents to the jetty via `DECK_SHARE` and they land at 19-21h; `puntFits` ends on `eastCloseHour() - hour > puntTripH(a) + PUNT_MIN_STAY_H`, so the crossing is refused on TIME and #128 measured 236 of 298 such offers dying there. #128 made the punt carry two and crossings actually FELL 62 -> 42, because a pair spends two of FAR_CAP's three — so the boat now has capacity it cannot fill and the supply that would fill it is standing on the deck at seven in the evening being turned away. Open the evening crossing. The honest question the brief is asking you to answer is which end gives: an evening trip that is legitimately shorter than a daytime one (there is nothing to look at on the eyot after dark, so the stay can be), or a jetty that is open later than the east half generally is. Pick one, price it, and say which.
successLooksLike: Over 10 seeds x 14 days the punt makes measurably more crossings than HEAD, at least some of them after sunset with the river lamps lit, and nobody is stranded on the eyot at the evening bell — every rider still comes home. Report crossings/day and people carried on both builds, the way #128 did.
avoid: Do not widen `eastOpen()` for the whole east half to buy this — that repopulates the plaza, the quay and the allotments as a side effect nobody briefed. LAWS: an arrival HOUR is a fact about GATE DISTANCE, not the source's window, and a choice must not be priced on something that gets re-priced on arrival. And #128's finding stands: a pair costs two of the cap, so measure PEOPLE CARRIED, not crossings alone.
